card: Polls more frequently in functional test sync helpers and RPC connection waits. Tests currently incur unnecessary idle time waiting for fixed sleep intervals to elapse when nodes finish syncing or RPC becomes responsive. The author reports test suite time reductions between 7% and 15% across multiple CI tasks and a 13% local wall time speedup.
evidence: Author benchmarks report a 13% reduction in local test suite wall time (110.8s to 96.4s at -j=18) and 7% to 15% reductions across several CI platforms (PR description).
problem: Functional tests spend unnecessary idle time sleeping between polling intervals while waiting for block/mempool sync or RPC initialization, slowing down local and CI test runs.

risk.why: Excessive polling frequency could increase CPU utilization or trigger test flakes under heavily loaded environments.

scope_notes: A very small 4-line adjustment in 2 test framework files.
summary: Increases the polling frequency in the functional test framework's node synchronization helpers and initial RPC connection wait loop. By reducing the sleep intervals between poll attempts, tests detect state transitions and RPC availability sooner.
